subject: Sprint Fund accelerator — credits, carryover and pricing floor
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@sprintfund.org>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-24T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint Fund program — credits and carryover question

Hi Irene,

Quick one — our Sprint Fund cohort (25 startups) is signing up for the Redwood starter package you shared at the demo. Two points came up internally: 1) can unused promotional credits be rolled forward to the next 90 days if they don't use them in month 1; and 2) can we get a cohort-level pricing floor (e.g., guaranteed max per-token rate) once they hit a certain run-rate?

We love the latency profiles but the founders are price-sensitive and some teams will be doing heavy embedding workloads. If we can get a modest carry-forward and a tiered floor that applies to the whole cohort, we can include Redwood as the preferred inference partner for the year.

Looping in procurement@ for anything legal/contracting. Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Liam
Director, Sprint Fund Accelerator
attachments: sprint-cohort-outline.pdf (pdf)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@sprintfund.org>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-24T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint Fund program — credits and carryover question

Hi Liam — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: we can offer a limited carry-forward on promotional credits for accelerators, and we can structure a cohort pricing floor, but there are a few trade-offs to align on (commit levels, burst capacity, and whether dedicated pools are required).

High-level options:
- Option A (No-commit carry-forward): Up to 25% of unused promo credits may be rolled forward once within a 60-day window; applies only to hosted accounts.
- Option B (Commit-based carry-forward + floor): If the cohort commits to $X/month in reserved usage for 3 months, we can roll forward up to 50% of unused credits and guarantee a per-token floor rate (e.g., $0.0009/token for text-gen and $0.00035/vector for embeddings) until the commit is satisfied. Dedicated pools get deeper discounts but require a minimum throughput.

Attached is a starter pricing doc (redwood-starter-pricing-v2.pdf) with the cohort SKU options and an example math for a 25-team cohort.

Next steps: if Sprint Fund prefers Option B, we should have Ben weigh in on reserving capacity and Monica on invoicing terms. Happy to do a 30-min sync this week.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0182
attachments: redwood-starter-pricing-v2.pdf (pdf)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@sprintfund.org>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-26T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint Fund program — credits and carryover question

Liam — appreciate the thoughtful framing. For cohort deals we usually present a two-track commercial:
1) Reserved cohort pool (recommended for heavy embedding workloads): monthly reserved commit + burst buffer. This unlocks a 15–25% discount vs hosted list and allows 50% carry-forward once per quarter.
2) Hosted with cohort privileges: lower up-front commit, 8–12% discount, and a 30% carry-forward cap with a 60-day window.

If Sprint Fund can provide an estimate of expected embeddings tokens per month (ballpark), I can run a quick model and show the unit economics. For signing speed, we can offer a one-time promotional uplift (extra 10% credits) if they finalize the cohort enrollment by May 6.

Monica, can you confirm billing cadence and whether we can do a single invoice to Sprint Fund with sub-accounts for each team?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: cohort-commit-template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: procurement@sprintfund.org
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint Fund program — credits and carryover question

Hi Ben, Irene —

Procurement here. We like Option B but need two confirmations before we proceed: 1) confirmation that carry-forward credit is non-transferable between different external programs, and 2) a simple clause showing the maximum aggregate liability for promo credits (our legal wants a cap). Also please confirm whether the one-time promotional uplift can be attached to the cohort-level invoice.

Can you also provide a draft MUP (master usage plan) that lists cohort-level SLAs and how excess usage is billed? If you have a short MUP doc we can review that speeds up legal.

Thanks,
Taylor Nguyen
Lead, Procurement — Sprint Fund
attachments: sprint-terms-redlines.docx (docx)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: procurement@sprintfund.org, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint Fund program — credits and carryover question

Taylor/Ben — thanks for the specifics. Confirmations below so legal has something precise to review: 

- Carry-forward scope: promo credits issued under the Sprint Fund accelerator enrollment are scoped to the cohort and are non-transferable to other promotional programs; unused credits can be carried forward once (up to the agreed percent) to the following 60-day window.
- Liability cap: Redwood's liability for promotional credits is capped at the total monetary value of credits issued under the cohort agreement (we'll include exact language in the MUP).
- Promotional uplift: the one-time +10% promotional uplift can be applied at cohort invoicing as a line-item credit; we'll reflect that on the invoice and within the MUP.

I attached a short MUP draft (sprint-mup-a1.docx) that includes SLAs (99.9% region-specific), burst handling, and overage billing rates. Monica — please confirm we can bill Sprint Fund on a monthly consolidated invoice with sub-account usage breakdowns.

If Sprint Fund is happy with the draft, I'll route the MUP to our legal and send the DocuSign link for signature. Proposed timeline: finalize terms by May 6 to secure the promotional uplift.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
attachments: sprint-mup-a1.docx (docx), redwood-starter-pricing-v2.pdf (pdf)
